title: Simple Past vs. Past Continuous
subtitle: Describe one action interrupting another in the past.
objectives: Use the past continuous for a longer, background action
Use the simple past for a shorter action that interrupts it

content.intro: Now that Simple Past is solid, let's add a new tense that works together with it: the past continuous, for describing what was already happening when something else occurred.

rules.heading: The pattern
rules.body:
• Past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) = the longer, background action, already in progress
  • Simple past = the shorter action that interrupts it, or happens during it
  • While + past continuous, simple past. / Simple past + when + past continuous.

examples: While I was walking to the park, I saw an old friend.
She was cooking dinner when the phone rang.
They were playing football when it suddenly started to rain.
I was watching TV when my brother came home.
He was reading a book while she was writing a letter.
We were having dinner when the power went out.

commonMistakes.wrong: He was played soccer when it started to rain.
commonMistakes.right: He was playing soccer when it started to rain.
commonMistakes.why: The past continuous needs the -ing form (playing), not the past form (played), after was/were.

commonMistakes.wrong: They was studying when the power went out.
commonMistakes.right: They were studying when the power went out.

commonMistakes.wrong: I finished my homework while I was watched TV.
commonMistakes.right: I finished my homework while I was watching TV.

commonMistakes.wrong: He ate dinner when she was arrived.
commonMistakes.right: He ate dinner when she arrived.
commonMistakes.why: A short, completed action (arrived) needs the simple past, not the past continuous — "was arrived" isn't a real form.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form (simple past or past continuous).

items.prompt: While I ___ (walk) to the park, I ___ (see) an old friend.
They ___ (play) football when it suddenly ___ (start) to rain.
items.explanation: "They" needs "were playing"; the sudden event is simple past.
The background action (already in progress) is past continuous.
The action in progress at that past moment is past continuous.

items.prompt: We ___ dinner when the lights went out.
items.explanation: The ongoing action interrupted by the event is past continuous.

items.incorrect: He was played soccer when it started to rain.
answer: He was playing soccer when it started to rain.
items.explanation: Past continuous needs the -ing form after was/were.

items.incorrect: They was studying for the exam when the power went out.
answer: They were studying for the exam when the power went out.

summary: Past continuous (was/were + -ing) = the longer, background action.
Simple past = the shorter action that interrupts it.
While + past continuous, simple past — or simple past + when + past continuous.
